answer: In mice, the distinction between papillary and reticular fibroblasts occurs early (about embryonic day 12.5), whereas human prenatal skin fibroblasts do not significantly express papillary fibroblast markers (COL13A1), suggesting this distinction emerges after 17 PCW in humans.
support_quote: Additionally, dermal fibroblast differentiation into histologically defined subsets (papillary and reticular) has been reported to occur early in mice (about embryonic day 12.5). Our human prenatal skin fibroblasts did not significantly express papillary fibroblast markers (for example, COL13A1) (Extended Data Fig. 5j), which suggested that the distinction between papillary and reticular fibroblasts emerges after 17 PCW.
